OnPlay.rationale: This is one of the more carefully ported cards in the pool and it holds up. Per iteration C# takes `PileType.Draw.GetPile(Owner).Cards.Where(!Unplayable).ToList().StableShuffle(Rng.Shuffle).FirstOrDefault()`, falling back to the UNFILTERED pile shuffled the same way when the filtered list is empty (Catastrophe.cs:25-30). The sim reproduces all four subtleties: it uses the named `Shuffle` stream via `stable_shuffled_cards(options, ctx.combat.combat_rng)`; it reverses the draw pile to the game's TOP-FIRST orientation first (colorless_skills.py:207) because StableShuffle's stabilising `list2.Sort()` leaves compare-equal cards in incoming order (ListExtensions.cs:22-31); it takes `[0]` after the shuffle rather than one uniform choice, so the draw COUNT matches (N-1 draws per pick); and `options = playable or pile` (colorless_skills.py:209) is exactly C#'s FirstOrDefault-null fallback. `is_playable` mirrors the Unplayable keyword. Citations re-pinned 2026-08-04; body unchanged since 2026-07-29 (the loop-bail fix below is the only content change this file underwent).

guards.what: Catastrophe.cs has NO loop-level bail-out (the loop runs the full CardsVar iterations unconditionally, combat-over is checked one level down inside CardCmd.AutoPlay AFTER the StableShuffle pick); the sim matches this today
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7), reconfirmed 2026-08-04 (stale-sweep re-audit): the sim's `on_play` loop (colorless_skills.py:206-213) has no `ctx.combat.is_over`/`is_dead` break of its own -- the only `break` in the loop is `if not options: break` (:210-211), the empty-pile case, which is the correct analogue of C#'s `FirstOrDefault()` returning null. Combat-over/player-dead is left to `auto_play_card`'s own internal check, matching `CardCmd.AutoPlay`'s `IsOverOrEnding || Owner.Creature.IsDead` guard (CardCmd.cs:53-56) running AFTER that iteration's pick is already made. So a StableShuffle (N-1 Shuffle draws) is still burned for every remaining iteration even after an auto-played card ends combat, on both sides. Pinned by test/test_card_residue_gaps2.py::test_catastrophe_burns_a_shuffle_for_every_iteration (verified present, 2026-08-04). No residual gap at this site.

Both also see any card the auto-play ADDED to the draw pile. Citation re-pinned 2026-08-04 (was :155).
